articles.title: 2 suspects wanted after 2-vehicle collision at St. Clair West and Jane
articles.summary: Two people were injured in a collision at St. Clair West Avenue and Jane Street on Friday afternoon. Officers responded to the intersection around 1:15 p.m. for reports of a two-vehicle collision. Toronto police say two occupants from one of the vehicles fled the scene on foot. They are described as males wearing all black […]

articles.title: Brampton family seeks community support to help get gene therapy for 2-year-old child with rare condition
articles.summary: A Brampton family is racing to raise millions of dollars for an American medical treatment that could help save their two-year-old child living with a rare genetic disorder after the province denied their out-of-country funding. Zoravar Singh has been diagnosed with a rare condition called AADC Deficiency. “His day starts with the medication and ends […]

articles.title: 2 workers critically injured in collision on Pickering construction site: police
articles.summary: Two workers are critically injured after being struck by a driver on a construction site in Pickering, police say.

articles.title: Stelco recalling 175 laid-off workers at Hamilton steel plant
articles.summary: Hamilton steelmaker Stelco is recalling its 175 workers that had been laid off earlier this fall.

articles.title: Feds, Ontario offering Stellantis 'aggressive package' to keep Brampton auto plant open
articles.summary: The federal and Ontario governments are mounting a last-ditch effort to save the Stellantis auto plant in Brampton by pitching the company possible survival "scenarios" and offering an "aggressive package" of support to make it happen.

articles.title: Stelco to recall 175 laid-off workers in Hamilton, Ont., on Dec. 1
articles.summary: HAMILTON — Stelco's American parent company has pledged to recall 175 temporarily laid-off steelworkers and repay their lost wages after weeks of federal pressure, including threats of legal action and the prospect of an investigation into anticompetitive conduct.

articles.title: Coroner's inquest begins in case of Mississauga man shot by police in 2020
articles.summary: A coroner's inquest into the death of a man shot in the head by police in Mississauga, Ont., is underway on Friday. Jamal Francique, a 28-year-old Black man, was shot during an attempted arrest outside his home on Jan. 7, 2020, and died in hospital days later.

articles.title: Ottawa, province hope ‘aggressive package’ can prevent Stellantis plant sale: Joly
articles.summary: TORONTO — A day after threatening to sue Stellantis to recoup federal cash given to the automaker, Industry Minister Mélanie Joly says she's still hopeful she can prevent the company from selling its Brampton, Ont., assembly plant to Roshel.

articles.title: Fatal fire at Scarborough home under investigation, chief says
articles.summary: The Office of the Fire Marshall has been notified, while Toronto's fire chief says it's too early to identify the cause of the fire.

articles.title: Construction underway on 2 bridges as part of Highway 413 project: Sarkaria
articles.summary: Construction is now underway on two new bridges to connect drivers to the upcoming Highway 413, a project that aims to reduce congestion in parts of the Greater Toronto Area, Transportation Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria said at a news conference in Brampton Friday.

articles.title: U of T music community celebrates beloved professor Mary Morrison's 100th birthday
articles.summary: Hundreds came together to celebrate the 100th birthday of a beloved music professor at the University of Toronto this week, along with her decades-long career teaching and performing opera.

articles.title: New Scotiabank Arena priority program puts members at the front of the line — at price tag of $2,500
articles.summary: Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment has launched a new program that gives members first access to tickets for Scotiabank Arena shows at a cost of $2,500 a year, but the price tag is not appealing to everyone.

articles.title: U of T rejects report saying school over-polices, under-protects Muslims, Arabs, Palestinians
articles.summary: A review of the University of Toronto's policies and practices has found the school has a "general pattern of over-policing and under-protecting" Muslims, Arabs and Palestinians, with a report laying out dozens of recommendations related to academic freedom, on-campus security methods, institutional autonomy and other concerns.

articles.title: Feds say Stellantis owes 'hundreds of millions' in subsidies, company offers $24M
articles.summary: Automaker Stellantis says it will pay back $24 million in federal subsidies after it announced plans to sell its Brampton, Ont. assembly plant — but Industry Minister Mélanie Joly says the company owes far more than what it is offering.

articles.title: Carney aware of 'some aspects' of Stellantis auto plant sale, but says company still broke deal
articles.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney says he had been informed of "some aspects" of Stellantis's plan to sell an idled Brampton, Ont., auto plant to Canadian armoured vehicle maker Roshel Inc., before the deal was announced.
